solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A range of binoculars?

parts.note: the span a pair of field glasses lets you see, read as the extent of sight they cover; the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.surface: A shopper asking about a product line of binoculars on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a catalogue of models, but it means the extent of what can be seen through them.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole area visible to an eye or lens is its extent of sight, which is what binoculars give you a range of.

clue.text: Sponsor a mad cardinal

parts.note: to sponsor something is to fund it
mad means mental, informally crazy

explanation.surface: Someone bankrolling a crazy senior churchman of the Catholic Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman, but here it is the adjective meaning chief, as in a cardinal rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of primary importance, a synonym for basic or essential.

clue.text: Drive, say, almost disappeared

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: almost signals the synonym is one letter short of complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: something that has disappeared is gone

explanation.surface: A car journey, for instance, that nearly vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone forward is to urge or spur them on, a phrasal verb of encouragement.

clue.text: Dud PMQs disputed in assembly of Dubai

indicators.note: in places the rearranged first group inside the rearranged second
an assembly of the letters of Dubai puts them together in a new order
disputed suggests these letters are argued over and rearranged

parts.note: PMQs is Prime Minister's Questions, the weekly session in the UK House of Commons

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome Prime Minister's Questions staged in a Gulf parliament proves a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: PMQs is Prime Minister's Questions, the weekly question session in the UK House of Commons. 'Dud' looks like an adjective but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a firework that fails to go off, hence any anticlimax or failure.

clue.text: Mess made by gunmen in US bank? Not half!

indicators.note: in means the gunmen sit inside what remains of the bank's name
not half means only one of the two halves of the bank's name is kept, the second

parts.note: Wells Fargo is a major American bank
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Chaos caused by armed robbers in an American bank, with an emphatic British 'not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it keeps just the second half of Wells Fargo. RA is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble, a synonym for a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Most of what's in golf bag is decreasing?

definitions.text: Most of what's in golf bag
definitions.meaning: most clubs carried by a golfer are the metal-headed numbered ones
read as de-creasing, the clue means is smoothing out wrinkles in clothes

explanation.surface: A golfer's bag is getting lighter, mostly emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decreasing' looks like getting smaller, but split as de-creasing it means pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry several numbered metal clubs, and someone pressing laundry with a hot appliance does this.

clue.text: Clumsy modern European stage worker

parts.note: in means fashionable or modern
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A present-day European theatre stagehand who is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' looks like a theatre, but it is a leg of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or polish, so awkward and gauche, is the sense shared with clumsy.

clue.text: Lousy egg container upended

indicators.note: upended turns the down entry upside down, so the container's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A rotten egg in a box that has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' looks like 'bad', but it means belonging to a louse.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg laid by a head louse is the louse's offspring in its casing, a pun on lousy.

clue.text: Two metals forming hook

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver; two metals are needed in all

explanation.surface: A pair of metals shaped into a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a sharp projection that catches on things, like a hook.

clue.text: Couple to keep port clear? It has strings attached

indicators.note: to keep means the pair holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to couple is to mate
Rio (de Janeiro) is a port
to clear is to net, as a profit

explanation.surface: A pair needed to keep a harbour free, with conditions attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' looks like conditions on a deal, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings from above literally has strings attached.

clue.text: Object, on reflection, when woman's injected white compound

indicators.note: injected means the woman goes inside the reversed word
on reflection means the word is seen backwards as in a mirror

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal
Agnes is a woman's name; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman is injected with a white chemical, and someone objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but it is the noun meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium oxide is a white powder used as an antacid, so it is a pale chemical compound.

clue.text: Get some wine, or lose it

definitions.note: to lose it is to lose one's temper

parts.note: to get something, as in understand it, is to see it
red is some wine, a glass of claret say

explanation.surface: Fetch some wine, or else someone will fly off the handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get some wine' reads as one errand, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To become suddenly furious is the idiom meaning to lose one's temper.

clue.text: Internet era transformed famous part of Olivier

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of these two words change into a new order

explanation.surface: The internet age has changed a celebrated role of Laurence Olivier.
explanation.walkthrough: Olivier played Archie Rice in John Osborne's play of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier's celebrated stage role in Osborne's play is its title character, a music-hall performer.

clue.text: Very neat, original music outlet dismissing tango

indicators.note: original suggests a fresh, inventive arrangement of the letters
dismissing means one letter is sent away from the phrase

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A tidy, novel record shop that no longer sells tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes one T from MUSIC OUTLET, and 'original' rearranges the remaining MUSICOULET.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing great attention to detail makes someone precise and very tidy.

clue.text: Shame to trigger cut in car racing

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the motor sport

parts.note: Indy is IndyCar, the American motor racing series

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to ignite is to set off or trigger

explanation.surface: A disgrace that set off cuts in motor racing.
explanation.walkthrough: INDY is short for IndyCar, the American open-wheel racing series.
explanation.definitionFit: Humiliation or loss of dignity is a kind of shame.

clue.text: Trace son about to obtain fashionable work

indicators.note: to obtain means to get hold of, so the word for about holds the other letters

parts.note: CA is circa, about
in means fashionable
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: A trace of a son trying to get trendy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives CA, circa, the abbreviation used with uncertain dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spark or the smallest amount of something is a trace.

clue.text: Faculty's revolutionary strategy half abandoned

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters read backwards
half abandoned means the second half of the word is dropped, keeping the first four letters

explanation.surface: A university department's radical plan is half dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half abandoned' keeps STRA of STRATEGY and 'revolutionary' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities group humanities subjects into one such department, so a faculty name.

clue.text: Companion for dam built at last in south of France

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south

indicators.note: at last picks only the final letter of the word built

explanation.surface: A dam was finally built in southern France, with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' looks like a water barrier, but it is a mare, a horse's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is a breeding mare, and her partner in breeding is a male horse kept for mating.

clue.text: Initiation here by holding wild parties? About time!

indicators.note: holding means the word by surrounds the remaining letters
about means wrapped around, so the rearranged letters go round the time
wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild parties held, and about time too!
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' gives APTISER, 'About' puts it round T as APTIS|T|ER, and 'holding' sets the result inside BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian initiation by baptism takes place in a church building or area containing the font.

clue.text: Mark's part of following into writing that's put out one November

indicators.note: put out means one letter is expelled
into puts the letter inside the word

parts.note: penning is writing
N is November in the NATO alphabet, one of them

explanation.surface: Part of a mark gets written off along with November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is the old German currency, the Deutschmark. 'into' puts F inside PENNING for PFENNING, and 'put out' removes one N.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the euro, the German Deutschmark was divided into a hundred of these small coins.

clue.text: It finishes on landing, in different ways

definitions.text: It finishes on landing, in different ways

parts.words: It finishes on landing, in different ways
parts.note: both a set of stairs and an aeroplane journey end at a landing, in two senses of the word

explanation.surface: Something that ends on touchdown, in various ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' works twice: a plane touching down, and the level floor at the top of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: An air journey ends when the plane lands, and a run of stairs ends at a level platform.

clue.text: Blight? It isn't heard of in parts of the country

definitions.meaning: a blight is a contamination or stain on something

definitions.text: It isn't heard of in parts of the country
definitions.meaning: the regional dialect contraction of 'it is not', as spoken in rural speech

explanation.surface: A plant disease unknown in some regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard of' looks like 'known', but it means the contraction 'tain't is spoken in regional dialects.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a corrupting stain or contamination, a synonym for a moral or physical spoiling.

clue.text: Get outside by drilling nonstop

indicators.note: drilling means boring into, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: eternal means unending, nonstop
X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: Getting out of doors by drilling without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is X, the times sign read as in 'six by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterior or outer, an adjective for something on the outside.

clue.text: Come to pass

definitions.meaning: to come to a place is to arrive at it
to pass something to someone is to hand it over, stretching out to give it

explanation.surface: The idiom 'come to pass', meaning happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'happen', but splits into two separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to get there, and stretching out to hand something over is passing it.

clue.text: Extra habit, not cape, a learner put on

indicators.note: put on means these letters are added at the end
not means the cape's letter is missing from the word

parts.note: an addiction is a habit
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: An extra habit, minus the cloak, is worn by a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like clothing beside 'cape', but it is an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is added over and above, so it is supplementary.

clue.text: Maybe vet fish hauled up

indicators.note: hauled up reads the down entry upwards, so the fish's letters run backwards

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Perhaps a vet checks a fish pulled from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vet' looks like a verb, check, but it is a veterinary doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A vet is an example of a doctor, informally called this.

clue.text: Perhaps Sally's East End stamping ground?

definitions.note: Sally is one example, from the fairground throwing game named after one such relative

indicators.note: East End Cockney speech drops the opening H

parts.note: a haunt is a favourite stamping ground

explanation.surface: Does Sally frequent a hangout in London's East End?
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game of throwing sticks at a target; Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sally's first name in the fairground game is this family title, so Sally is perhaps one.

clue.text: Call cameraman out of house, one in Bletchley Park?

parts.note: to cry is to call out

indicators.note: out of means the house's letters are taken from the cameraman

parts.note: a photographer works a camera

explanation.surface: Phone the cameraman to leave the house, one at Bletchley Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Bletchley Park in England was the WWII codebreaking centre where Enigma was cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Codebreakers who worked on wartime ciphers at Bletchley Park were experts in codes.
